s: Distributed SQL that shards itself and survives node/datacenter loss while speaking Postgres-flavored SQL.
w: Data lives in ranges (Raft consensus groups) replicated 3x, auto-split and migrated for balance. Transactions use serialized timestamps ensuring external consistency across ranges. Nodes form one logical cluster; losing minority replicas keeps data readable/writable. SQL layer sits atop the KV layer enabling joins/distributed transactions transparently.
use: Globally distributed OLTP needing strong consistency without hand-sharding
Financial ledgers, inventory, billing where correctness > raw speed
Cloud-native multi-region active-active with serializable isolation
Escape hatch from manual shard management as growth continues
avoid: Latency-tiny-budget paths crossing regions (commit-wait costs ms)
Budget-tight projects - resource footprint is significant

pat.d: Serializable transactions simplify appending ordered events consistently.

pits: Hot-spotting on sequential keys - hash or scatter prefix high-write tables
Cross-range txn latency - co-locate related data via INTERLEAVE/follower reads
tips: Position vs Spanner (open-source analog), vs Vitess (manual shard mgmt eliminated), vs mongo (consistency guarantees)
